mainEntity.name: How do professionals ensure the repaired seam blends into existing wall texture?

acceptedAnswer.text: Matching existing wall texture requires identifying the application method and feathering the perimeter carefully. Common textures include knockdown, orange peel, and hand-troweled finishes. After the drywall seam is coated flush and sanded, a contractor applies a matching texture spray or trowel mix diluted to the correct consistency, matching the droplet size or stroke pattern of the room. Feathering the new texture several inches into the existing undisturbed wall avoids a noticeable patch line. A dedicated drywall primer must seal the fresh patch before applying two coats of matching paint.
acceptedAnswer.description: Technicians identify the specific texture style, feather the spray or trowel pattern several inches past the repair, and apply primer to ensure the paint sheen matches evenly.
